scope: Independent source review of D23 red guard and notice-resolution fix, including notice producers, relay contexts, organization lifecycle, and unrelated refusal preservation. No tests or browser run in this lane.

A_live_ui.reason: The fix can retire the notice in source, but no live panel observation in this review establishes the overlay disappears or that Save becomes hit-testable. The original Save attempt remains ambiguous and must not be retried.

findings: The producer census finds NO_ORGANIZATION only at capture-ladder queue.listNeedsYou; failDbCall marks a resolution condition only when classifyDbFailure returns no_workspace. Other database failure kinds and manually pushed notices receive no condition and survive retireResolved.

The cross-context path preserves the whole Notice object: non-sidepanel pushNotice sends it through DB_FAILURE_NOTICE and the sidepanel NoticeHost adds the received object without reconstruction, including resolvesWhen. Sidepanel-local failures add directly to the same store.

NoticeHost resolves in both timing orders: the storage-change listener retires tagged notices when a non-null organization arrives, and a notice-list effect rereads the current organization so a delayed refusal arriving after selection is retired. The pending read is canceled with an alive guard on effect cleanup. Sign-out/null changes do not retire notices.

retireResolved filters only notices with the requested condition. The test covers an existing tagged refusal plus an unrelated error, and a late tagged refusal after selection; recorded red receipt attributes both failures to the intended stale-notice assertions rather than an import or timeout failure.
limits: The focused unit guard is root-reported green, not run by this peer. Its mocked organization listener does not exercise Chrome's real cross-context storage event or runtime message relay; those paths are supported by source inspection and remain part of the native read-only retest.

checks: Independent source review only; no tests, browser, or build launched.
